angle: The hard direction of Nash-Williams–Tutte as a good characterisation (TONCAS): a real k-forest packing algorithm runs live, greedily grows, runs a breadth-first exchange/augmenting search over EDGES when an edge fits nowhere, applies swap chains end-first — and when the search finally closes with nothing found, the set A of edges it reached is collapsed into the partition P = components of (V,A), whose cross-edge count is then recounted from scratch by a verifier sharing no code with the solver and shown to fall below k(r-1). The user watches an algorithm's failure turn into a short, independently checkable proof of impossibility, and lands on the dichotomy: either k labelled spanning trees or one sparse partition, never neither and never both, both witnesses polynomially checkable.

libraries.name: d3
libraries.role: the only DOM/data-join layer. Every SVG scene is a pure function of a step snapshot re-rendered through selection.join with stable keys: edges keyed by edge index (stroke = forest colour, stroke-dasharray = forest dash, a separate low-alpha halo layer for 'reached by the search' and a stronger one for the F_i-cycle currently being walked), vertices keyed by vertex id, partition blobs keyed by part id, and the BFS search structure keyed by edge id. Also supplies d3.polygonHull (input to the rounded-hull blob path), d3.line().curve(d3.curveCatmullRom.alpha(0.6)) for the augmenting-chain overlay through edge midpoints, d3.group for BFS depth rows, d3.range/d3.mean, and the survey/brute-force table joins. d3.transition is DELIBERATELY UNUSED so it never overlaps Anime.js.

libraries.name: animejs
libraries.role: the only animation engine. (1) The §3 flood: anime.timeline() with a shared `update` callback chaining four tweens on a plain state object {t, shown} — reached-set highlight, blob hardening (t drives both the Minkowski pad and the interior-edge opacity), cross-edge reveal, then a round:1 count-in of cross edges — writing back into the 'harden' range input each frame so the manual slider and the playback are the same control. (2) The §1 weld arcs staggered in by (treeIndex*(r-1)+weldIndex)*55ms. (3) A short opacity pulse on the main SVG at every swap/found step. Chosen over GSAP (claimed by artifact 03) and over d3.transition (would duplicate D3's job).

libraries.name: katex
libraries.role: all notation, via one [data-tex] (inline) / [data-tex-d] (display) sweep with throwOnError:false and an idempotence guard. Renders: the theorem as an iff with \underbrace-labelled 'witness A' / 'no witness B exists' halves, the definition of e_G(P), the toll k(r-1) decomposed by \underbrace into trees x welds, the three-line necessity chain, the quoted exchange identity sum|F_i| = (|E|-|A|) + k(n-c(A)), its rearrangement into |E|-|A| < k(r-1), and the O(|E| alpha) / O(|E|) checking costs on the two dichotomy cards. All 20 .woff2 faces vendored.

building_blocks: DSU(n): path-compressed disjoint-set forest with find/union/count()/labels(); labels() returns {part:Int32Array, r} with parts renumbered 0..r-1 in first-appearance order — one primitive reused for per-forest component tests, for components of (V,A), and for both independent verifiers
buildDSUs(g,k,owner) -> [DSU x k]: rebuild all per-forest union-finds from the flat owner array, so forest state is never stored redundantly and a scrubbed snapshot is always self-consistent

forestPath(g,owner,i,a,b) -> [edgeIdx] | null: the unique a..b path inside forest i, by BFS over only the edges owned by i — this is the 'cycle that adding f to F_i would close', i.e. the eviction candidate list
forestVertexPath(g,owner,i,a,b) -> [vertexIdx]: same path as a vertex sequence, for drawing

runPacking(g,k) -> {steps, owner, status:'packed'|'stuck', cert, target, reached}: THE ENGINE. Greedy growth, then multi-source BFS over the exchange digraph on EDGES seeded with every unused edge, then end-first application of the augmenting swap chain, then the certificate. Every step is pushed with a full Int32Array snapshot of owner plus the live reached-set labelling, so timeline scrubbing is an exact pure function of step index and no state is replayed

step trace vocabulary {kind, chapter, head, body, owner, idx, total, target, ...}: kinds init | add | block | search-start | expand | found | swap | augmented | exhausted | dead | cert | done, grouped into 6 chapters (grow, block, search, swap, dead, cert) that drive a chapter rail; head/body are human narration generated from the real numbers

exchange-search labelling: Map(edge -> {parent, forest, depth}) where `forest` is the forest whose cycle was walked to reach this edge (== the forest the edge currently sits in, i.e. the one it would be evicted from); the label map unwinds directly into the swap chain [{edge, from, to}]
applyChain end-first: for s = len-1 down to 0, owner[chain[s].edge] = chain[s].to — valid because BFS yields a SHORTEST chain in the exchange digraph and therefore one with no shortcuts

verifyForestsOnly(g,k,owner) -> {per:[{size,comps,acyclic,spanning}], allAcyclic, total}: the from-scratch integrity re-check run after every augmentation (throws on a cycle) and also the data source for the forest ledger
buildCertificate(g,k,reachedSet) -> {part, r, members, crossE, interiorE, cross, need, deficit, violated, A}: collapse components of (V,A) into parts, split E into interior/cross, compute k(r-1)

verifyPackingWitness(g,k,owner) and verifyCertificateWitness(g,k,part): the two INDEPENDENT verifiers — they share no code path with runPacking, take only the witness, and return {ok, notes:[{t,ok,v}]} rendered as a checklist. This pair is the whole 'good characterisation' payload
bruteForceMin(g,k) -> {slack, r, cross, need, part, enumerated}: exhaustive restricted-growth enumeration of all set partitions (n<=11), the ground-truth cross-check for the emitted certificate

mkGraph(o): graph descriptor {id, name, n, edges:[[u,v]], pos:[[x,y]], labels[], blurb} + derived lab(v), ename(e) ('u–v'), and view:[x,y,w,h] — a viewBox computed from the position bounding box with padding, so each preset fills its panel instead of sharing one guessed world box

islandsGraph(cnt,label): geometry-first construction — place cnt pentagon centres on a ring, orient each pentagon so one vertex faces the centroid, emit the cliques, then choose each bridge as the geometrically nearest cross-island vertex pair. The edge list is DERIVED from the layout, so the drawing and the combinatorics can never disagree
ring(cnt,cx,cy,R,phase) and clique(ids): the two layout/edge-list primitives every preset is built from

blobPath(pts,pad): exact Minkowski sum of the convex hull with a disc — hull orientation fixed by signed area, outward normal (dy,-dx)/|d| per edge, an SVG A-arc of radius pad at every joint, with explicit circle (1 point) and stadium (2 points / degenerate hull) cases

GraphView(selector): the reusable scene. Layer order blob / halo / edge / chain / hit / vertex / note; setGraph(g) also stamps g.view onto the svg viewBox; render(st) takes {owner, reached:Set, path:Set, chain, blobs, blobT, crossSet(+crossSet.rank), crossShown, note, hover} and rebuilds everything by data-join. Interior edges fade with blobT, cross edges are revealed one at a time by rank, and a transparent 14px stroke per edge carries the hover tooltip

SearchTree(selector): the growing BFS structure — edges grouped by depth into rows, node width fitted to the widest row, links drawn as vertical cubics coloured by the forest whose cycle was walked, node border coloured by the edge's current owner, the edge being examined filled black
certBlobs(g,cert): part member positions + centroid + label, with the size suffix suppressed for singleton parts (the degenerate all-singletons certificate would otherwise be ten '(1)' labels)

renderCertBar(cert): the e_G(P) vs k(r-1) meter — a fill to the actual count, a hatched deficit band with a critical-red leading edge, an ink tick at the toll, plus a per-unit tally row of k(r-1) squares (filled = a real cross edge, dashed outline = the shortfall)

forestSwatch(i,w) / legendHTML(k,extra): forest identity as colour + dash pattern + glyph (bullet/square/triangle), so identity is never colour-alone; extra slots for the search-halo and cross-edge roles

transport controller {run, at, playing, timer, speed}: first/back/play/forward/last + a 5-position speed table + a scrub range, with per-step dwell time longer on swap/block/found/dead steps than on greedy adds
chapter rail: one button per chapter, jumping to the first step with that chapter, auto-disabled when a run contains no such step (e.g. a graph that packs successfully has no 'maximum' phase)
checklist primitive (ul.chk): 20px glyph column + claim + right-aligned tabular value, glyph ✓/✗ coloured by status — used for both witness verifiers and the shown/waved lists
pill(ok|bad|neu): dot-glyph-plus-words status chip so verdicts never rely on hue alone
renderMath(root): one-pass KaTeX sweep over [data-tex] / [data-tex-d] with a data-done idempotence guard

fold-down page skeleton: hero + numbered .beat sections separated by hairlines, .split / .split.even / .split.rightwide two-column grids with `min-width:0` children collapsing at 1000px, a `.sticky` left column so the live graph stays on screen while the right column is read, and an IntersectionObserver reveal whose failsafe adds BOTH `.in` and `.instant` (transition:none) so a screenshot or a misfiring observer can never leave the page blank or mid-fade
computations: the full k-forest packing algorithm: greedy growth by per-forest union-find, multi-source BFS exchange search over the edge exchange digraph, end-first swap-chain application, with a from-scratch acyclicity re-verification after EVERY augmentation that throws if a cycle was ever created
the unique F_i-cycle closed by each blocked edge, computed by BFS inside the forest and displayed edge by edge as the eviction candidate list

K4, k=2: greedy fills F1={ab,ac,ad}, F2={bc,bd}, edge cd is blocked in both; the search walks the F1-path ac·ad and the F2-path bc·bd, finds ac addable to F2, and the two-link chain ac:F1->F2, cd->F1 completes the packing at 6 = 2·3 — a genuine augmentation on the very smallest example
K5, k=2: 8 = 2·4 packed out of 10 edges (2 spare), reached after 2 exchange searches
K6, k=3: 15 = 3·5 packed using every one of the 15 edges — a perfect decomposition, found by 3 exchange searches and 9 swaps

C6, k=2: greedy consumes all 6 edges (F1 spanning, F2 a single edge), no homeless edge is left, so the search never wakes, A = empty, and the certificate degenerates to r=6 singletons with 6 < 2·5 = 10
Petersen, k=2: 14 greedy adds, then one successful exchange search consumes the 15th edge; all 15 edges spent against a target of 18, A = empty, certificate r=10 with 15 < 18

2 x K5 + 1 bridge, k=2: n=10, m=21 >= 18 so the headcount test passes; the search reaches 20 of the 21 edges, the components of (V,A) are the two islands, and the certificate is r=2 with e_G(P)=1 < 2·1=2

3 x K5 + 3 bridges, k=2: n=15, m=33 >= 28 so the headcount passes with slack and r=2 passes too; packing tops out at 27, the exhausted search reaches exactly the 30 island edges, the components of (V,A) are the three islands, and the certificate is r=3 with e_G(P)=3 < 2·2=4 — verified against the identity (33-30) + 2(15-3) = 27, exactly the packing achieved
the exchange identity checked numerically on every stuck run: (|E|-|A|) + k(n-c(A)) printed beside the packing actually achieved, with a live pass/fail marker — it holds on all four failing presets

independent re-verification of the emitted partition: r = number of distinct labels, a fresh pass over E counting crossings, the product k(r-1), and the strict inequality — computed from part[] alone with no reference to the forests or the search
independent re-verification of every successful packing: per forest, union-find over its edge class asserting n-1 edges, acyclic, exactly 1 component

brute-force minimum of e_G(P) - k(r-1) over ALL set partitions for every preset with n <= 10 (K4 15, K5 52, K6 203, C6 203, Petersen 115975, 2xK5 115975 partitions), compared against the emitted slack — agreement on every row

offline stress test behind the design (not shipped in the page): 3904 random multigraphs, n 3-8, k 1-3, solver verdict vs brute-force partition truth — 0 mismatches, and every emitted certificate was the minimum-slack partition, not merely a valid one
the toll widget: k(r-1) recomputed for r in 1..7, k in 1..3, with r-1 welds drawn per tree
interactions: §2 graph picker (K4 / K5 / K6 / C6 / Petersen / 2xK5+bridge / 3xK5+3bridges) and k picker (1/2/3): re-runs the entire algorithm, rebuilds the trace, rescales the timeline, relabels the legend, and cascades into §3's certificate scene and §4's dichotomy cards
§2 transport: restart, step back, play/pause, step forward, jump to end; a 5-position speed control (0.4x-3.2x) with swap/block/found/dead steps dwelling ~2.3x longer than greedy adds
§2 scrub slider over every step of the run (up to 149 steps on the 3-island graph) — an exact pure re-render from that step's snapshot, never a replay

§2 chapter rail (grow / blocked / search / swap / maximum / verdict): jumps to the first step of a phase; chapters that never occur in the current run are disabled (a graph that packs has no 'maximum' phase)

every step simultaneously updates: the graph (forest colours and dashes, reached-set halos, the F_i-cycle path being walked, the augmenting-chain overlay through edge midpoints), the forest ledger (edges/n-1 spend bar and component count per forest), the total against k(n-1) with a status pill, the BFS search-structure panel, the narration panel and the scrolling trace log
hover any edge in either graph: tooltip with its name, its current forest, whether the search reached it, and whether it crosses the partition
§3 'flood the reached set' plays the Anime.js timeline: highlight A, harden the components into blobs while interior edges recede, then count the cross edges in one at a time against the toll
§3 'harden' slider scrubs the same morph by hand at any position, cancelling the timeline; 'reset' returns to 0
§1 r slider (1-7) and k slider (1-3): redraws the cluster strip and the k(r-1) welding arcs, and rewrites the toll sentence (including the vacuous r=1 case)
§4 survey table: computed on load for all 7 presets; clicking any row loads that graph and k back into §2/§3 and scrolls to the machine
§4 dichotomy cards: whichever witness the live graph actually has lights up and fills with its verification checklist; the other is dimmed and stamped 'not this graph'
§5 'run the enumeration': runs the full set-partition brute force in-page for every preset with n <= 10 and tabulates partitions enumerated, true minimum slack, emitted slack, and agreement
assets: lib/fonts/KaTeX_*.woff2 (all 20 faces: AMS, Caligraphic Bold/Regular, Fraktur Bold/Regular, Main Regular/Bold/Italic/BoldItalic, Math Italic/BoldItalic, SansSerif Regular/Bold/Italic, Script, Size1-4, Typewriter)
gotchas: ESM-only builds fail from file:// (origin null => CORS), so all three libraries are plain UMD dists loaded by classic <script> tags — animejs 3.2.2 is the last UMD line (v4 is ESM-only and would have failed); verified by loading in headless Chrome over file:// WITHOUT --allow-file-access-from-files and asserting zero exceptions and zero console errors

D3 and Anime.js both animate, which violates the one-job-one-library rule if used naively. The split enforced here: D3 owns data-joins, scales, geometry and shape generators and NEVER calls .transition(); Anime.js owns every tween and drives D3 re-renders from its update callback. Without that discipline the two fight over the same attributes
katex.min.css references fonts/KaTeX_*.woff2 by relative path; without all 20 faces vendored the maths silently falls back to a system font with wrong metrics
KaTeX does not lay out correctly in quirks mode, so the document starts with <!DOCTYPE html> and a real <head>/<body>

the reveal-on-scroll pattern leaves the page blank in full-page screenshots and wherever the IntersectionObserver misfires; a plain setTimeout failsafe is NOT enough either — under Chrome's --virtual-time-budget the class lands but the 0.55s CSS transition never completes, so the page screenshots at ~15% opacity. The failsafe must add BOTH the visible class and a `transition:none` class

related: under --virtual-time-budget, computed styles on elements whose class changed after load can be read STALE (the chapter-rail button that lost .now still reported the .now font-weight and box-shadow, while the button that gained it reported none). classList was correct throughout — verify class state via a DOM probe, not by eyeballing a headless screenshot, and remove transitions from any element whose state you need to screenshot

a single guessed 760x560 world box wastes most of the panel for compact graphs; deriving the viewBox from each graph's own position bounding box plus padding is what makes every preset fill its stage. The padding must cover the widest blob offset AND its label, or the certificate blobs clip at the panel edge (54 was too tight; 64 works)

any text drawn at fixed svg coordinates breaks once the viewBox is per-graph — the status note had to be anchored to view[0], view[1]+view[3] instead of (18,26), and moved to the BOTTOM of the box because at the top it collided with the first partition blob

an outward polygon offset cannot be faked by scaling hull points away from the centroid. The blob outline is a true Minkowski sum with a disc: hull orientation normalised by signed area, outward normal (dy,-dx)/|d| per hull edge, and an SVG A-arc at each joint — with explicit circle and stadium fallbacks, because the degenerate all-singletons certificate consists entirely of one-point parts

part labels placed above the blob work for a 5-vertex island and are unreadable clutter for ten singleton parts; the fix is centroid placement with a surface-coloured paint-order:stroke halo for multi-vertex parts, a short offset label for singletons, and no '(1)' size suffix on singletons

three K5 islands laid out on a ring of radius 180 with island radius 96 overlap visibly and put all three bridge endpoints in a crowded centre — the certificate's three-part structure becomes unreadable. Radius 198 with island radius 80 separates them cleanly and turns the three bridges into a legible central triangle, which is exactly the picture the certificate is about

the greedy edge order matters for the narrative, not the answer: scanning edges in index order fills F1 to spanning first and only then struggles with F2, which is what produces interesting exchange searches instead of a symmetric fill. The final verdict is order-independent (confirmed against brute force), but the trace is not

the exchange chain can only be applied wholesale because BFS yields a SHORTEST path in the exchange digraph (a shortcut would contradict minimality). A best-first or DFS search would silently produce chains whose earlier swaps invalidate later ones — the from-scratch acyclicity assertion after every augmentation exists precisely to catch that class of bug and was kept in the shipped code

the certificate construction has a degenerate branch that is easy to get wrong: when greedy consumes every edge there are no homeless edges, the search never runs, A is EMPTY, and the components of (V, empty) are the n singletons. That is still the correct optimum (C6 and Petersen both match brute force), and the resulting certificate is exactly the crude m >= k(n-1) test — the page names this rather than special-casing it away

the fourth categorical slot (yellow) fails the all-pairs CVD and normal-vision floors against slot 2 (orange) on the light surface, so k is capped at 3 and status-red is reserved for the certificate/violation role and never used as a forest colour; the three forest colours were run through the palette validator under --pairs all --mode light against this page's surface (worst CVD dE 9.2, worst normal-vision dE 24.0) and each also carries a dash pattern and a glyph

slot-3 aqua sits at 2.74:1 on the light surface, below the 3:1 bar, which triggers the relief rule — every forest is therefore directly labelled (F1/F2/F3 chips with glyph and dash in the legend and the ledger) and the survey table doubles as the table view

a stuck greedy run is not a proof, and it is very easy for a page like this to imply that it is. Both the failure callout in §2 and the two 'refuses to say' notes in §5 exist to block that reading, and the verdict text is always sourced from the recount, never from the solver's state
sticky left columns need `position:static` restored under the mobile breakpoint, or the graph pins itself awkwardly once the grid collapses to one column
